newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise, seen holding for next few days.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise, seen holding for next few days.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Monday amid positive sentiment and dealers saw little likely to change unless Thursday's U.S. jobless data produced surprises.
The market would watch Wednesday's meeting of the Fed's FOMC meeting, a dealer said, but saw no reason to worry as there were no expectations of an interest rate rise.

At 0920 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 112.60, yielding 6.08 percent, up from Friday's 112.50. The seven percent 2007, due to become the benchmark on September 1, climbed to 105.21, yielding 6.29 percent, from 105.20.
The 2006 bond's yield gap to the 10-year bund narrowed one basis point to 42 bp and the 2007 gap to the bund did likewise, closing to 63.
The crown firmed slightly, to 3.8073 to the mark from 3.8075. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
